architecture.title: My standard: Hexagonal Architecture

It's like building a house where you can change the decoration or the type of air conditioner without touching the load-bearing walls: the application is more stable, easier to test and ready to evolve.

facturello.title: Facturello - Simplified invoicing for freelancers
facturello.description: Invoicing micro-SaaS for freelancers and solopreneurs: elegant invoices, online payments through multiple providers (NotchPay, KPay, PayPal), automatic reminders and a built-in AI assistant to manage your entire business in one place.
facturello.longDescription: Facturello is far more than an invoicing tool: a complete platform for freelancers and solopreneurs. It lets you create elegant invoices, collect payments online through multiple payment providers (NotchPay, KPay, PayPal), automate overdue invoice reminders, manage clients and subscribe to paid plans. A conversational AI assistant (LangChain/LangGraph, RAG, MCP server) assists with writing and analysis. The application is built on Astro 7 for rendering, Svelte 5 for interactivity, Tailwind CSS 4 for the UI, and Supabase with Prisma 7 for data persistence.
features: Create professional invoices in 60 seconds
Online payments via multiple providers (NotchPay, KPay, PayPal) with webhooks and transaction deduplication
Automatic email reminders for overdue invoices
Conversational AI assistant with document RAG and MCP server
Paid plan subscriptions with automatic upgrade/downgrade
MFA and WebAuthn passkeys for strengthened authentication

items: Astro 7: Static rendering and partial hydration for optimal performance
Svelte 5: Reactive interactive components with runes
Tailwind CSS 4: Modern responsive utility styling
Supabase: authentication (MFA, WebAuthn passkeys), PostgreSQL and storage
Prisma 7: Type-safe ORM with structured migrations
NotchPay, KPay & PayPal: online payments with webhooks and deduplication
Inngest: automatic reminders and subscription expiration
LangChain & LangGraph: conversational AI assistant with document RAG
Transactional emails with Resend
Professional PDF generation
Vercel deployment, Docker image available

fluidio.title: Fluidio Shop
fluidio.description: Full-stack e-commerce marketplace connecting sellers, buyers and affiliates: Flutter mobile app, Flask API, real-time WebSocket, mobile money payments (Orange Money, MTN MoMo) and shop geolocation.
fluidio.longDescription: Fluidio Shop is a multi-actor marketplace designed for the Cameroonian market, and Central Africa more broadly. The ecosystem includes a Flutter mobile app (buyer, seller and affiliate spaces with dedicated themes), a hexagonal Flask API (~25 business modules), a real-time service (messaging, presence, notifications) and multi-environment Docker orchestration. Payments rely on Orange Money and MTN MoMo with webhook confirmation and push notifications.
features: Three user spaces (buyer, seller, affiliate) with profile conversion
Private shops: shop code, QR code, deep links and customizable theme
Orange Money and MTN MoMo payments with webhooks and push notifications
Real-time messaging: conversations, typing indicator, read receipts
Affiliate program: referral, commissions and withdrawals
Real-time geolocation of shops and products

pepites-academy.title: Pépites Academy
pepites-academy.description: Complete football academy management platform: website and back-office (SvelteKit), REST API (Flask), field mobile app (Flutter) with QR attendance scanning, report cards and SMS — the training division of K-Sport Agency.
pepites-academy.longDescription: Pépites Academy grew from a showcase website into a complete academy management platform with four components: a SvelteKit website with a back-office (academics, sessions, attendance, report cards, applications, SMS), a Swagger-documented Flask REST API, a Flutter field mobile app (QR attendance scanning, annotations, PDF report cards) and a NestJS/Socket.io real-time microservice. All components follow a hexagonal architecture.

QR scanning of stadium entries and exits
Field mobile app: annotations, workshops, PDF report cards with radar charts
SMS module (NEXAH gateway) with CSV/Excel import and bulk sending

Offline mode with resilient synchronization (web and mobile)

Redis planned for horizontal scaling

facturello.Astro: I picked it for partial hydration: pages load almost instantly, because JavaScript ships only where I actually need interactivity.
facturello.Svelte: I love how compact it is: compiled components with no virtual DOM give me a reactive, lightweight UI.
facturello.Tailwind CSS: I use it to iterate fast: the whole design system lives in the markup, responsive included, with no stylesheets to maintain.
facturello.Supabase: It saved me from building a backend: auth, PostgreSQL and storage are managed, so I focus on the product.
facturello.Prisma: I can't work without its typing anymore: the schema acts as a contract and keeps my changes safe.
facturello.Inngest: I use it for everything that must run in the background: reminders and expirations fire on their own, with automatic retries.
facturello.Vercel: I deploy without thinking about it: every push is in production within minutes, zero configuration.

linkyza.Next.js 16: I chose it for the App Router and hybrid rendering: the marketplace stays well-ranked while offering rich interactions.
linkyza.TypeScript: With ~40 business models, I don't take chances: strict typing lets me refactor with peace of mind.
linkyza.Supabase: I grouped the essentials in one place: managed PostgreSQL, auth and file storage in a single service.
linkyza.Prisma: The schema is 40+ models, and Prisma keeps me type-safe end to end with controlled migrations.
linkyza.Inngest: I rely on it to make payments reliable: transaction sync and emails, with automatic retries.
linkyza.NotchPay: It's the gateway built for Africa: Mobile Money payments in FCFA and vendor payouts — I haven't found anything as fitting.

k-sport.SvelteKit: I wanted a premium, very fast site: server-side rendering and smooth transitions do the job.
k-sport.Tailwind CSS: I built the visual identity with it: a utility design system, consistent from the first to the last screen.
k-sport.Supabase: For a showcase site, no dedicated backend needed: I manage content and contact forms with it directly.
k-sport.SEO: I spent time on it on purpose: meta tags, sitemap and solid performance so clubs and athletes can find us.

meetly.Next.js: I liked keeping a single codebase: the app and its API routes live together, it simplifies everything.
meetly.Supabase: I lean on it for OAuth, 2FA and PostgreSQL: meetings, teams and recordings all live there.
meetly.LiveKit: I chose open-source, self-hostable WebRTC: no dependency on a proprietary video service.
meetly.Gemini AI: I use it to transcribe and summarize meetings automatically, straight through the Gemini API.
meetly.Inngest: It orchestrates my asynchronous transcription-then-summary pipeline, without me handling failures by hand.
meetly.AWS S3: I store recordings there: durable, cost-effective, and pre-signed URLs keep access secure.

medin-plus.Angular: For a complex business app, I prefer its structured, typed approach: it stays maintainable over time.
medin-plus.Laravel: I know its PHP ecosystem well: mature, with an expressive ORM, perfect for the API.
medin-plus.Supabase: Medical data is sensitive: managed auth and RLS to properly isolate each doctor.

hugbot.SvelteKit: I wanted an instant chat experience: its fine-grained reactivity and built-in server data fit perfectly.
hugbot.Hugging Face: It gives me access to the best open-source LLMs (DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama) through a single, affordable API.
hugbot.Supabase: I persist conversations and auth with it: everything lands in near real time without a home-made backend.
hugbot.Prisma: I kept a crystal-clear data model: conversations, messages, settings — nothing superfluous.
hugbot.LangChain: I use it for RAG: embeddings, context retrieval and prompt orchestration, without reinventing the wheel.
hugbot.Inngest: I wired it to sync settings and send notifications, without ever blocking the user.

fluidio.Flutter: I didn't want to write two apps: a single Dart codebase gives me Android and iOS with native performance.
fluidio.Flask: I chose it lightweight and modular: the hexagonal architecture lets the API grow cleanly.
fluidio.PostgreSQL: For orders, commissions and stock, I want integrity: its relational constraints guarantee it.
fluidio.Soketi: I self-host it: Pusher-compatible real time without paying per connection.
fluidio.Redis: I put it between instances: shared cache and messaging for the real-time service.
fluidio.Docker: It guarantees dev, staging and prod stay identical, and I deploy with one command.

pepites-academy.SvelteKit: I merged the public website and back-office into a single app: fast, and well-ranked.
pepites-academy.Flask: I exposed every business module as REST, with Swagger: the other components plug in easily.
pepites-academy.Flutter: On the field, the network isn't guaranteed: I designed the app offline-first, attendance scans even without a connection.
pepites-academy.NestJS: I added it for real time: a modular microservice, ready to hook into an event bus.
pepites-academy.PostgreSQL: Attendance and report cards can't have errors: I need its integrity guarantees.
pepites-academy.Docker: I reproduce the same backend from dev to prod: no more 'it worked on my machine'.

poweralert.Tauri: I wanted a 2 MB app, not an embedded Chromium: the system webview was more than enough.
poweralert.Rust: For low-level battery access, I wanted reliability: no memory leaks, no crashes.
poweralert.Astro: It's an app that lives in the background: I gave it a near-JavaScript-free UI, discreet and fast.
poweralert.TypeScript: It secures the exchanges between the UI and the Rust commands through Tauri IPC.
